subject: Mini-session billing and tiered-discount mechanics for short-lived chat flows
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: procurement@acme-retail.com
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Mini-session billing and tiered-discount mechanics for short-lived chat flows

Hi Sarah / John,

Thanks again for walking through the integration yesterday. One topic that came up and that your product team flagged was how we meter and price a high volume of very short chat interactions (what we're calling "mini-sessions") — examples: quick SKU lookup in a retail UI, one-question FAQ popovers, or realtime autocomplete confirmations where each interaction is typically <= 8 tokens and returns in under a second.

Quick summary of constraints and ask:
- These interactions are very low token-count but high QPS; the customer is worried about per-call minimums and rounding causing unexpectedly high bills.
- They want a predictable unit for forecasting and to explore a tiered discount for large counts of mini-sessions.

Three proposals from Redwood to consider (high level):
1) Token-minimum approach: keep standard token metering but apply a reduced per-call minimum for mini-sessions (e.g., 3-token floor instead of the full session minimum). Rounding: round up to nearest whole token.
2) Micro-batch aggregation: during short time windows (configurable, e.g., 30s), group mini-session calls from the same user/device into a single "micro-batch" for billing, effectively amortizing overhead.
3) Mini-session SKU: offer a bulk SKU (price per 1k mini-sessions) with pre-negotiated tiers and automatic unit conversion on invoice.

What we'd like from you:
- Baseline monthly estimate of mini-session volume (rough bucket is fine: <10k / 10-50k / 50-200k / >200k).
- Preference among the three options above and any hard constraints (e.g., cannot delay aggregation >100ms).

Attached is a short usage sample (acme_mini-session_usage_sample.csv) and a mock invoice preview that demonstrates how each option would change line items. We'll loop in billing to provide concrete numbers after we get your volume bucket.

If helpful, we can set up a 30-minute call with Rishi (billing) and Neha (customer success) to run through the math.

Thanks,

Mateo Alvarez

Hi Mateo,

Thanks — this is exactly the set of options we wanted to see. A couple quick clarifying questions before we pick a preferred approach:

1) Do mini-sessions count against context-length for the user’s conversation? For example, if the UI opens a 3-token mini session and then later the user asks a full question, does that 3-token call increment the conversation context for subsequent calls?

2) For the micro-batch aggregation, what is the failure semantics if a batch window closes without any other calls (i.e., will a lone call still be billed at the micro-batch minimum)?

3) On the SKU approach: can we get an example of how discounts step-up with volume and whether unused pre-paid bundles roll over?

Our rough volume expectation initially is 20k–40k mini-sessions / month per region (US). We may test with a low-volume pilot first.

Appreciate the proposed call — John and I can do next Tuesday afternoon.

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Turner <sarah.turner@acme-retail.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-03T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mini-session billing and tiered-discount mechanics for short-lived chat flows

Hi Sarah — great questions, thanks for the volume estimate. Below are concrete answers + a couple of illustrative calculations based on the CSV you sent.

Short answers:
- Context accounting: mini-sessions are accounted as normal token events. If you want to avoid those calls incrementing a longer-lived conversation context, we can configure the integration to use ephemeral contexts (does not persist into later conversational requests). That is an integration-side flag; we can set it per route.
- Micro-batch failure semantics: if a micro-batch window closes with only one call, that single call is billed normally under the micro-batch rules (i.e., it will still receive the micro-batch amortization if configured with a per-window floor). We can set a per-window minimum to protect against pathological single-call windows.
- SKU questions: proposed step tiers (example):
  * 0–9,999 mini-sessions / month: base rate (no extra discount)
  * 10,000–49,999: 10% off base per-mini-session unit price
  * 50,000–199,999: 18% off
  * 200,000+: 25% off and eligibility for a committed-cap price
Rollovers: we generally do not permit rollovers on usage-based SKUs. If you prefer rolloverable pre-paid bundles, we can offer a commitment model instead (committed monthly minimum with true-up).

Illustrative math (from attached CSV sample):
Scenario A — no aggregation, token-floor = 3 tokens per call
  - 1 mini-call = 3 tokens billed (if it actually used 1–3 tokens, rounded up to 3)

Scenario B — micro-batch window = 30s, no per-window floor (aggregate all calls in window)
  - If 20,000 calls arrive in bursts averaging 5 calls/window and each call averages 3 tokens: billed tokens approx = windows * (sum(tokens per window)) = 4,000 windows * 15 tokens = 60,000 tokens (same as A in this pattern)

Scenario C — mini-session SKU at negotiated price (example pricing):
  - 20,000 mini-sessions @ $7 / 1k mini-sessions = $140 (apply tiered discount if applicable)
  - Equivalent token billing depends on token price; SKU gives simpler forecasting and typically yields a predictable per-month charge.

Rounding rules: token meters are always rounded up to the nearest whole token. For micro-batch aggregation, we sum raw token counts first, then apply rounding only at the final token sum to avoid excessive per-call rounding overhead.

Next steps we suggest:
1) Pilot with micro-batch aggregation enabled and a 30s window for 30 days to observe natural burst patterns.
2) If Acme wants strict predictability, pilot the mini-session SKU for a month at the 10k–50k tier.
3) If you confirm commitment levels we can produce a pricing attachment and sample invoice for legal.

I've attached the CSV and a quick sample invoice (proposed_invoice_preview.pdf) which shows side-by-side numbers for the three options. Happy to review live on Tuesday — Mateo, please share available slots.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Billing & Pricing | Redwood Inference
